earlier_scan.source_named: Nagy, Naomi (2000), Faetar (Lincom Europa, Languages of the World/Materials) — grammar of Faeto/Celle Francoprovencal; not online. Wikipedia Faetar article has no stress statement.

new_statements.quote: 2.2. Faetar stress. Stress always appears on the rightmost non-schwa vowel of a word. The stressed syllable is always one of the last three syllables in the word. However, stress is not on a fixed syllable, counting from the left or from the right, nor is it consistently on either an odd or an even syllable. Furthermore, stress may be on either an open or closed syllable [...] One binary foot, a generalized trochee (Kager 1993), is built at the right edge of the word. Some words have one extrametrical syllable at their right edge, but no more than one. [...] Several arguments have shown that Faetar is a language in which stress is lexically marked and schwa is not a phoneme

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is lexical within a right-edge three-syllable window: it falls on the final, penultimate or antepenultimate syllable and cannot be predicted from syllable count, parity or weight; surface-wise it is the rightmost full (non-schwa) vowel, but Nagy argues schwa is itself the reduced reflex of unstressed vowels (post-tonic vowels are categorically schwa, pretonic variably), so stress position (plus at most one lexically extrametrical final syllable) is what is stored. Certain morphological classes (past participles, many infinitives) are oxytone; Italian loans keep the Italian stressed syllable even after final-syllable deletion. The local Sportello 2006 grammar (pp. 12-13) independently lists tronche/piane/sdrucciole words and calls 4th-from-last stress 'pochissime o quasi nulle' (only verb+enclitic strings).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing stated; analysis builds a single foot at the right edge ('If we assume that only one foot is built on each word'), pretonic syllables unfooted.
new_statements.exceptions: Preantepenultimate stress essentially absent (Sportello 2006: only enclitic strings like bà-je-sce-me 'baciami'); raddoppiamento sintattico after word-final stressed vowels; variable word-final deletion more frequent in antepenult-stressed words (Nagy & Reynolds 1997); pretonic full-vowel/schwa free variation (tawəlinə ~ tawolinə).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level primary stress; examples are isolated lexical words in phonetic transcription; RS experiment uses picture-naming in isolation and in sentence frames. Francoprovencal source language has a two-syllable window; Faetar's three-syllable window attributed to Italian/Apulian contact.
new_statements.identity_note: Nagy's 'Faetar' covers the Francoprovencal of both Faeto and Celle di San Vito (Foggia, Apulia) = Glottolog faet1240 exactly (a dialect node under Francoprovencal/Arpitan fran1260). The Sportello 2006 grammar describes the Faeto variety specifically. Note the parent-language catalog entry fran1260 (Kasstan 2015, Lyonnais) records a two-syllable (final/penult) lexical window; Faetar differs in having a three-syllable window (antepenult possible, via Italian/Apulian contact and loans).

sources.note: Sec. 2.2 'Faetar stress': stress always on the rightmost non-schwa vowel; always one of the last three syllables; not on a fixed syllable from either edge; may be on open or closed syllable; analysis: one generalized trochee at right edge plus at most one lexically extrametrical syllable; paper argues stress is lexically marked (schwa = reduced unstressed vowel, post-tonic vowels categorically schwa, pretonic variably); past participles and many infinitives have word-final stress; Italian loans keep Italian stress even after final deletion.

sources.note: Sec. I 6 'L'accento tonico' (pp. 12-13): words are tronche (final stress: feleccettà, bun-tà, par-là), piane (penult: sa-là-me, ve-stí-te), sdrucciole (antepenult: túm-me-le, bròc-che-le, scà-re-pe) or bisdrucciole (4th-last: 'pochissime o quasi nulle', only verb+enclitic strings bà-je-sce-me, dí-sce-me-le); no predictive rule given; I 7: tonic vowels are marked with a written accent, omitted on disyllabic paroxytones where it 'cade naturalmente sulla prima sillaba'.
